benchmarks.name: owasp-benchmark-java
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Applicable rules have 24 false positives and detect 172 of 660 expected vulnerable cases.

benchmarks.name: nist-juliet-java-1.3
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Command and SQL recall remain low. Juliet files mix good and bad methods, so this corpus supplies case recall and location corroboration, not TN or standalone precision.

benchmarks.name: gosec-testutils-go
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Detection outside the rules' published scope is expected: G115 is general integer conversion while the rule covers parse-then-downcast, and G402 covers cipher suites and TLS versions the rule does not claim. The corpus supplies precision evidence and in-scope recall, not whole-rule recall. G204 measures the new cra-go-shell-command-injection rule. It detects 0 of 7 vulnerable cases with 0 false positives on the 6 safe ones. Five of the seven use a program name taken from os.Args or a variable, which is arbitrary program execution rather than shell injection and is outside the rule's stated scope. The two that do use the shell form take the command from a function parameter, which gosec treats as tainted by default and this rule does not, because it requires a recognised source. The corpus supplies precision evidence for this rule and no in-scope recall evidence.

benchmarks.name: nist-juliet-c-cwe377
benchmarks.license_note: Public domain under 17 USC 105; CC0 1.0 for any foreign rights, per the SARD suite page
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Recall evidence only. Juliet's non-vulnerable variants for this category often still call the same name generator and fix the problem with O_EXCL on the later open, so its safe cases are safe on a different axis than this rule reports on and cannot supply a precision denominator. The 36 skipped files are Windows variants that need Windows headers.

benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Strong for this rule: 34 of 34 vulnerable cases detected with no finding in a Good method. The suite covers only 3 of the 8 C# rule CWEs and its HTTP source idiom is System.Web rather than ASP.NET Core, so the other C# rules get no evidence from it.

benchmarks.name: codeql-rust-cwe295
benchmarks.license_note: MIT, per the github/codeql repository LICENSE. Fixture text is reused as ground truth; the CodeQL engine is not run.
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: All 10 alerts whose argument is the literal true are covered, with no finding on a good line. The 7 uncovered alerts pass a variable or const, which the rule does not resolve, the same non-literal boolean boundary the Go TLS rule has.

benchmarks.name: codeql-js-cwe078
benchmarks.license_note: MIT, per the github/codeql repository LICENSE. Fixture text is reused as ground truth; the CodeQL engine is not run.
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: The 96 alert lines are the whole CodeQL command injection tree, which is dominated by sinks these rules never claimed: execa, cross-spawn, ssh2, opener, @actions/exec, promisified exec wrappers, and spawn or execFile argument arrays. 11 alert lines are inside the published scope of cra-javascript-exec-injection, exec or execSync resolved from child_process with the command built by concatenation or template interpolation, and all 11 are covered. Read the covered figure against that 11, not against 96. The tree carries no good-marked lines, so this benchmark measures recall only and gives no false positive signal.

benchmarks.name: owasp-benchmark-python
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Default tier only. Five of eight applicable CWEs reach 100 percent precision (cookie, command injection, SQL, eval) with open redirect at 82 percent. Deserialization sits at its corpus ceiling of 60 percent, where every remaining false positive keeps a sink byte-identical to a true positive and differs only in dead-code dataflow. Path traversal and XSS score zero because the corpus is a Flask application and those default rules target Django sinks; a Flask response rule covering that shape ships at experimental tier.
benchmarks.cwe_alias_note: The corpus labels eval and exec injection cases CWE-94, a class-level weakness that MITRE 4.20 does not list as mappable. The rule declares CWE-95, the precise child. The alias records that relationship for scoring without weakening the rule's own mapping.
benchmarks.score_tier_note: Scores the default tier only, since the measurement is about what ships without a flag.

benchmarks.name: nist-sard-php-cwe78
benchmarks.label_correction_note: The corpus labels by directory, safe or unsafe. Two generated shapes carry the wrong label and both are detected mechanically. A safe case that applies its sanitizer to the misspelled variable $tained leaves the tainted value reaching the sink and is scored vulnerable. An unsafe case that reassigns the tainted variable from $sanitized, which it never assigns, kills the taint and is scored safe. 192 of 2496 cases, 7.7 percent, are affected.
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Measures cra-php-command-superglobal only. Precision is far below the promotion bar. Modelled sanitizers are shell escaping, numeric casts and numeric filter_var. Validation by regular expression is deliberately not suppressed because the corpus contains permissive patterns it correctly labels unsafe. Allowlist comparison via in_array is the remaining tractable precision work. Findings on htmlspecialchars, htmlentities and addslashes cases are a deliberate disagreement with the corpus: none of those neutralise shell metacharacters.
benchmarks.license_note: The repository carries no LICENSE file. Every generated case embeds its own grant in a header comment: Copyright 2015 Bertrand STIVALET, permission granted without written agreement or royalty fee to use, copy, modify and distribute the software and its documentation for any purpose, provided the copyright notice and disclaimer paragraphs appear in all copies. The corpus is read during scoring and no case is redistributed with this package.

benchmarks.name: nist-sard-php-cwe89
benchmarks.label_correction_note: The corpus labels by directory, safe or unsafe. One generated shape carries the wrong label in this directory. An unsafe case reassigns the tainted variable from $sanitized, which it never assigns, so the taint is killed and the case is scored safe. 96 of 9552 cases, 1.0 percent, are affected. The misspelled $tained sanitizer shape present in the CWE-78 directory does not occur here.
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: Measures cra-php-sql-superglobal-taint only. Precision is far below the promotion bar, and the rule also produces 15 findings on phpMyAdmin production code, so it fails the real-code half of the bar independently. Recall was 0 percent before this measurement because the corpus executes through mysql_query, the legacy extension removed in PHP 7, which the rule did not cover. Escaping functions are deliberately not modelled as sanitizers: see the rule's sanitizer_analysis.

benchmarks.name: nist-juliet-csharp-cwe89
benchmarks.license_note: Public domain under 17 USC 105; CC0 1.0 for any foreign rights, per the SARD suite page
benchmarks.promotion_blocker: The labelled corpus measurement passes the precision threshold, but the experimental rule matches request and SQL APIs by written name. Exact application-versus-framework ownership is not proven, so the stronger adversarial binding condition remains unsatisfied.
benchmarks.promotion_note: Measures cra-csharp-sql-request-taint. Every finding lands in a Bad method and none in a Good method. Recall is 189 of the 549 files whose BadSource is an HTTP read; the undetected variants carry the flow across a method or file boundary, which intrafile taint does not follow. The remaining files in this directory take their BadSource from a socket, file, database, console, environment variable or network client, which are not request data and correctly produce nothing. The discriminating controls are the Good methods: GoodG2B puts a hardcoded string into the same bad sink and GoodB2G puts the bad source into a safe sink, and both are silent.

benchmarks.name: eslint-js-no-loss-of-precision
benchmarks.promotion_note: The narrow default rule detects only assigned odd integer literals above the binary64 safe-integer boundary. It detects 24 of 46 official invalid cases and none of 79 official valid cases. The remaining invalid cases are outside the declared scope and stay false negatives rather than weakening precision.
